data.assessment: Under rush load the town delivered 216.6 of 228 orders on time (0.95) with nothing unfinished. Robots still spent 1824 s blocked, and pickup lateness (10.0) causes most late deliveries. A never parks on the road yet is blocked longest (843 s), so B and C (about 48 road waits each) are effectively serving their own customers at A's expense. A is now the worst-off company at 0.93–0.94 on-time, C leads at 0.99 but carries the most penalties (11.0), and road violations are dominated by overstays (deadline:release 16).

proposals.title: Tighten blocking_guard: evict a parked robot when 2 (not 3) robots wait behind it
proposals.rationale: Blocked time is 1824 s and A, which never parks, absorbs 843 s of it. Pickup deadlines (10.0 violations) are the main source of lateness, so evicting parked robots sooner should free intersection 8 and raise on_time_deliveries and A's floor rate. Conditions changed since period 1: this period has a rush (25 s order interval), so blocking matters more, and this is a test under that load, not a re-run of the vote override the human deferred. Expected votes: A yes, since A gets less blocking and has no penalties. B and C are likely no, because evictions are Major sanctions on their parked robots, so the amendment probably fails at quorum 2 unless their on-time gains outweigh the penalties.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
assumptions: Evicted robots move off intersection 8 rather than re-parking immediately on another blocking node.
A's high blocked seconds are caused by B and C robots parked on the road, since A records zero road waits.
unknowns: Whether the extra Major eviction penalties outweigh B's and C's on-time gains in their utility.
Whether more frequent evictions add travel time that hurts pickup deadlines during the rush.
Whether this is the same lever as period 1's option 1, whose cost to C the human asked to have explained.

proposals.title: Shorten hold_limit from 60 s to 50 s under rush load
proposals.rationale: Overstays (deadline:release 16.0) are the largest road-violation cause, and 1824 s of blocking is concentrated during the rush. A shorter hold limit should push parked B and C robots off intersection 8 sooner and help A's pickups. In period 1 this lever measured -1.2 on-time (2/5 seeds) under normal load. What has changed is the rush, where blocking costs more, so this re-test checks whether the result differs under load. Votes: A likely yes. B and C are likely no if their overstay penalties rise without offsetting on-time gains.

regulation_proposals.title: Lower vote.quorum from 2 to 1 (narrowly scoped, conditional on this period's measurement)
regulation_proposals.rationale: In D1 the human named a narrowly scoped quorum-revision proposal with an impact statement as the proper next step. This proposal does that, but should be adopted only if the block_k measurement this period shows a clear customer gain blocked by B's and C's votes. Impact: customers, especially A's (the current floor at 0.93), would get amendments that cut blocking. A gains on-time deliveries and utility. B and C lose their individual veto and may face more eviction and overstay penalties; C's utility fell by about a third in a similar case in period 1. The precedent concern also remains: any single company could then carry amendments, including ones that hurt the other two, so the invariants become the only protection. A safer alternative is to raise invariants.min_company_on_time_rate alongside this change.
assumptions: The invariants (min company on-time rate 0.6, max unfinished 2) and the min_improvement gate remain as safeguards when one vote suffices.
Customer gains measured on 5 seeds are representative.
unknowns: Why C's utility dropped sharply under period 1's option 1, which the human asked to have explained first.
Whether the increase in road violations seen in period 1 has safety relevance.
Whether a single company would use quorum 1 to pass amendments that harm the others' customers.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Allows customer-positive amendments that currently fail on B's and C's votes.

predictions.subject: metric:min_company_on_time_rate
predictions.note: A, the floor company, benefits most from less blocking.

predictions.subject: metric:utility@C
predictions.note: C bears more penalties under amendments it would have vetoed.

predictions.subject: metric:sanction_total
predictions.note: Blocking-reduction amendments mainly work through penalties.
